title: Maintenance Order
context: Plant Maintenance › Preventive & Breakdown Maintenance (PM) › Maintenance Order

cards.title: Database schema architecture, entity bindings, and data models of fMaintenanceOrder
cards.body:
fMaintenanceOrder is the primary work order management interface operating within the PM module.
Header attributes map to EAM.EAMMaintenanceOrder with primary key OrderId and DocNo.
Task details persist in EAM.EAMOrderTaskDetail capturing TaskId, AssignedTo, and ScheduledDates.
Material demands map to EAM.EAMOrderItemDetail storing ItemId, WarehouseId, and RequiredQty.
Resource allocations persist in EAM.EAMOrderResourceDetail and skill mapping tables.
Safety permit linkages map to EAM.EAMOrderPermitDetail and check list audit tables.
Entity state transitions follow DocumentStatus flags Initial, Release, and Authorized.
Optimistic concurrency relies on ModifiedDate and ModifiedBy columns verified on save execution.
Shared custom fields interface through masterdata.customfieldssave during transaction commit.
Foreign key constraints enforce referential integrity against equipment, employee, and task masters.
Audit triggers record modification history in EAM.EAMOrderAuditDetail for compliance tracking.
Atomic transaction boundaries ensure order headers, tasks, and item demands commit synchronously.
Clustered indices on OrderId and DocNo optimize query performance across large maintenance datasets.
Foreign key relationships bind work order tasks to task master tables and employee rosters.
Non-clustered indices on EquipmentId accelerate order history retrieval during preventive maintenance analysis.
Relational constraints and clustered indices optimize query execution plans during high-volume database operations.
Database triggers intercept unauthorized data manipulation attempts and enforce strict referential boundaries across schemas.

cards.title: Stored procedure bindings for search, load, save, and delete in fMaintenanceOrder
cards.body:

Record searches execute through EAM.EAMOrderSearchData returning paginated order headers based on criteria.
Selected order details load via EAM.EAMOrderLoadData and EAM.EAMOFillValues stored procedures.
Task, resource, and item details load through EAM.EAMOFillValuesDependent routines.
Transaction persistence is orchestrated by the master save routine EAM.EAMOSave.
Task detail persistence executes through EAM.EAMOrderTaskDetailSave within the transaction.
Record deletion invokes EAM.EAMODelete which validates downstream reporting and issue references.
Lookup values and responsible person lists populate using EAM.EAMOFillValues procedures.
Custom validation routines execute through EAM.EAMOrderCustomValidation handlers.
Stored procedures return structured error codes handled by the application exception layer.
All persistence procedures execute within serialized transaction blocks to maintain data consistency.
Audit logging procedures capture user credentials and execution timestamps across all order modifications.
Stored procedures utilize table-valued parameters for efficient task and material line insertions.
Structured catch blocks capture relational database errors and execute explicit transaction rollbacks.

cards.title: Validation logic, Boolean conditions, and error triggers in fMaintenanceOrder
cards.body:
fMaintenanceOrder enforces strict scheduling and integrity rules prior to saving in the database.
OrderDivision != EquipmentLocation triggers validation errors halting transaction execution on save.
EstimatedStartDate < DocumentDate fires an immediate date validation refusal.
EstimatedEndDate < EstimatedStartDate aborts processing with duration sequence exceptions.
EstimatedDuration <= 0 triggers numeric validation failure for planned labor hours.
TaskStartDate < OrderEstimatedStartDate or TaskEndDate > OrderEstimatedEndDate fires range errors.
Empty TaskName or empty RequiredQty on item rows halts saving with mandatory line errors.
DocumentStatus == Authorized halts save attempts with Authorized MaintenanceOrder can't be updated.
Multi-level authorization bypass attempts abort processing with authorization level errors.
Validation checks execute sequentially within client pre-checks and server validation procedures.
Missing equipment selections or inactive task masters trigger foreign key validation exceptions.
Structured error messages identify the exact line item and column violating business constraints.
Server procedures re-verify all Boolean conditions to ensure data integrity against direct API calls.
Failed checks raise custom error codes mapped to localized user error messages in the interface.
Rollback handlers reverse all intermediate variable states when any rule triggers an exception.
Relational constraints and clustered indices optimize query execution plans during high-volume database operations.

cards.title: Detail line replacement architecture and atomic transaction boundaries
cards.body:
Editing existing fMaintenanceOrder documents utilizes a detail replacement mutation pattern in the database.
Existing child rows in EAM.EAMOrderTaskDetail and EAM.EAMOrderItemDetail are purged on save.
Current UI grid rows are inserted anew within a single atomic database transaction.
If any task or item insertion fails, the entire transaction rolls back preserving original data.
Cascade routines update source MaintenanceRequest statuses from Open to In-Progress.
Material requisitions in Inventory schema update open reservation balances against the order.
Historical change logs capture prior order attributes before detail row replacement executes.
Concurrency timestamps prevent detail replacement if another session modified the record.
Atomic transaction scopes guarantee that work orders and inventory demand stay synchronized.
Line replacement commits synchronously with document header updates within a single transaction.
This mutation pattern prevents partial configuration saves and eliminates orphaned task records.
Foreign key cascades verify that item codes in demands exist in masterdata.mItemMaster.
Transaction isolation levels prevent concurrent transactions from reading partially replaced rows.
Relational constraints and clustered indices optimize query execution plans during high-volume database operations.

Transaction logs capture user connection parameters and execution timestamps to maintain comprehensive enterprise auditability.

cards.title: Concurrency controls, optimistic locking, and referential barriers in PM
cards.body:
fMaintenanceOrder enforces optimistic concurrency to maintain consistency in multi-user environments.
When saving, the procedure compares the client ModifiedDate with the database record timestamp.
If another session modified the order, the server returns Someone updated this record.
Referential integrity barriers prevent document deletion once downstream processes engage.
If actual work reporting records exist in EAM.EAMMaintenanceReporting, deletion is blocked.
If storekeepers have issued materials in Inventory.IMaterialIssue, deletion is disallowed.
Authorized orders cannot be deleted or un-authorized through standard application interfaces.
Order cancellation routines must be utilized to terminate unwanted jobs formally in the system.
Security audit tables log all authorization, update, and deletion attempts with user session data.
Database triggers enforce referential barriers across EAM, Inventory, and masterdata schemas.
Optimistic locking prevents lost updates during simultaneous job scheduling by maintenance planners.
Audit trails preserve complete historical snapshots of maintenance orders for statutory compliance.
Referential integrity barriers protect historical maintenance orders from accidental administrative removal.
Database triggers ensure child records in task tables purge synchronously on draft removal.
Transaction rollback handlers ensure that partial deletions never leave orphaned records in child tables.
Relational constraints and clustered indices optimize query execution plans during high-volume database operations.
